resourceSpecification.description: Relationship. Model:'https://github.com/tmforum-apis/TMF664_ResourceFunctionActivationConfiguration/blob/v4.0.0/TMF664-ResourceFunctionActivation-v4.0.0.swagger.json#/definitions/ResourceFunction/properties/resourceSpecification'. Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within an enterprise's infrastructure or inventory. They are typically consumed or used by services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content and information, and technology components. A ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of Resource. In essence, a ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that is based on a particular ResourceSpecification. In TMF this is a ResourceSpecificationRef object; here the NGSI-LD id of the referenced ResourceSpecification entity (urn:ngsi-ld:ResourceSpecification:<tmf id>). Inline values and reference metadata (href, name, @referredType) are not kept.
